issue.title: Non-reproducible build after changing android installation

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
My android build failed because I didn't have the right SDK packages installed. After installing them, I had to run `bazel clean` for the changes to be picked up:

```
$ bazel build src/main/java/com/mycompany/android/...
ERROR: missing input file '@androidsdk//:build-tools/22.0.1/zipalign'.
$ echo y | /opt/android-sdk/tools/android update sdk -u -a -t android-21,build-tools-22.0.1
$ bazel build src/main/java/com/mycompany/android/...
ERROR: missing input file '@androidsdk//:build-tools/22.0.1/zipalign'.
$ bazel clean
$ bazel build src/main/java/com/mycompany/android/...
<success>
```

Cleaning is a trivial workaround, so this isn't a serious problem itself, but it might lead to more insidious reproducibility bugs.

issue.title: Building @repo//:all or @repo//:... don't work

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Working on #352, I noticed that @foo//:all doesn't work (individual targets do).  I was attempting to fix this in TargetPattern, but the change just kept getting bigger so I figured I'd file a bug and get back to it later.  Basically:
- TargetPatternResolver should probably take PackageIdentifiers instead of Strings
- So PackageIdentifier should be moved to cmdline (and its dependencies on ExternalPackage and Label.SyntaxException severed). 
- All implementations of TargetPatternResolver should be modified to expect PIs.

issue.title: Example bazel build fails due to "unexpected short read from file"

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
I compiled and installed Bazel on a 64-bit VM running 32-bit Debian 8.0.

```
$ uname -a
Linux devel-libca-skeggsc 3.16.0-4-686-pae #1 SMP Debian 3.16.7-ckt9-3~deb8u1 (2015-04-24) i686 GNU/Linux
```

When I create a new workspace and try to build in it, it fails with a very odd error. To make sure that it wasn't an artifact of the workspace, I rebooted the virtual machine, created a new workspace, removed `~/.cache/bazel`, and ran an example build command in the new workspace:

```
skeggsc@devel-libca-skeggsc:~/new-workspace$ bazel build examples/java-native/src/main/java/com/example/myproject:hello-world
Extracting Bazel installation...
..................................
ERROR: no such package 'external': Error encountered while dealing with the WORKSPACE file: Unexpected short read from file '/home/skeggsc/.cache/bazel/_bazel_skeggsc/install/c856fa2026bd5b1d370edcd52403a9ea/_embedded_binaries/jdk.WORKSPACE' (expected 8800387990324, got 820 bytes).
INFO: Elapsed time: 1.896s
```

This is the error that I've been getting from Bazel.

I checked the size of the named file:

```
skeggsc@devel-libca-skeggsc:~/new-workspace$ wc -c /home/skeggsc/.cache/bazel/_bazel_skeggsc/install/c856fa2026bd5b1d370edcd52403a9ea/_embedded_binaries/jdk.WORKSPACE
820 /home/skeggsc/.cache/bazel/_bazel_skeggsc/install/c856fa2026bd5b1d370edcd52403a9ea/_embedded_binaries/jdk.WORKSPACE
```

I also notice that 8800387990324 (the length that it thinks the file should be) is equal to `2^43 + 2^32 + 820`. This seems suspicious.

Any idea why I'm getting this error?

issue.title: strip_prefix leads to invalid dep includes

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body: When getting includes by deps, `strip_prefix` is not honored. This way it results in `-Isystem external/lua/src` (with e.g. the actual path being `external/lua/lua-5.2.4/src`). Either the error lies in extracting with the `lua-5.2.4` (which is `strip_prefix`) path or with not handling `strip_prefix` for deps.

issue.title: changing the length of build_files of new_* rules fails

labels.name: P1
labels.description: I'll work on this now. (Assignee required)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
After changing the length of the build file for a new_\* rule, Bazel re-reads the old length of bytes from the file. If it got smaller, this fails. If the file got longer, the bytes beyond the original length are ignored.

I think this is related to @haxorz's recent changes to read/parse/etc BUILD files less often.

For example, starting with the following files:
WORKSPACE:

``` python
new_local_repository(
  name = 'test_repo',
  path = '/tmp/test_repo',
  build_file = 'test.BUILD',
)
```

test.BUILD:

``` python
cc_binary(
  name = 'test',
  srcs = ['test.cc'],
)
```

/tmp/test_repo/test.cc:

``` c++
int main() { return 0; }
```

`bazel build @test_repo//:test` succeeds as expected. However, running `echo foobar >> test.BUILD` and then `bazel build @test_repo//:test` again succeeds even though it shouldn't. It fails like it should after a `bazel shutdown`.
